subject: reference-reduction

created_trees.objective: À partir du candidat T1 le plus rapide, intégrer le mécanisme de réduction intra-bloc du candidat T2 dans la hiérarchie tuilée de T1. Préserver le calcul complet sur GPU, la correction pour toutes les entrées et les contraintes de scratch/flux par défaut; mesurer le programme intégré entier.
created_trees.stop_condition: Rejeter tout résultat incorrect. Si le programme intégré correct ne bat pas T1 selon le même protocole, garder T1 comme meilleur G; ne retenir la combinaison pour confirmation que si sa mesure le justifie.
created_trees.subject: Combinaison mesurée de la hiérarchie T1 et de la réduction intra-bloc T2

active_architecture.warning: Model wall times overlap research; do not add them to campaign wall time

children.objective: In src/candidate.cu, compare scratch-backed, non-atomic reduction hierarchies for large n: a coalesced tiled first pass plus one final device sum, and a three-stage or other multistage variant if the partial count makes the final pass costly. Sweep useful per-CTA work and block sizes; do not assume fewer stages always wins. Keep this experiment distinct from T3 by avoiding global atomic output accumulation. Preserve tail safety, scratch bounds, and correctness for every valid input. Validate all required sizes and compare repeated whole-call timings; do not use external DeviceReduce-style libraries.
children.subject: Non-atomic reduction hierarchy depth and tile sizing

children.objective: Isolate the cost of reduce0's intra-block shared-memory tree: compare a warp-level reduction using valid CUDA sync intrinsics and a correct inter-warp combination, optionally against an allowed CUB block primitive. Hold global input mapping, block geometry, and pass structure fixed during comparisons. Ensure participating lanes use correct masks and synchronization, including tail blocks. Report correctness and repeated whole-call timings. Preserve a correct modular implementation even if it does not beat the full baseline alone, since it may combine differently with a changed hierarchy; do not claim a combination is faster without measuring it.
children.subject: Intra-block reduction primitive and synchronization

children.objective: Test a one-kernel large-n path: zero out with cudaMemsetAsync on the default stream, then have each CTA reduce its input tile locally and contribute exactly one sum with atomicAdd. Sweep CTA tile size to expose the tradeoff between input work and atomic contention, but avoid per-element atomics and global partial-buffer reduction in this path. Compare the full memset-plus-kernel path with a non-atomic two-kernel control using the same first-pass tile and block mapping, so initialization and finalization costs are visible. Use current input data, no extra allocations, and no stale scratch dependencies; preserve correctness and tail safety for every valid input. Report repeated whole-call timings even if this approach loses.
children.subject: Single-kernel atomic finalization with explicit output initialization
